title: Multi-agent systems and subagents
trust_boundary: Before: one model, one context, one set of permissions, one transcript. After: an orchestrator hands tasks, context and sometimes credentials to other agents and treats what they return as input to its next step.
Messages between agents are model-written text. A subagent that read untrusted content can pass an injection upward or sideways.
Agents can hold different tools and permissions, so delegation can widen what one request reaches.
No single transcript shows the whole action, and errors compound across hops.
context_questions: Which agents exist, what tools and permissions does each hold, and who can add one?
Are any agents run by another party or on another vendor's model?
What does an orchestrator pass down: the whole context, or only the task?

threats.title: An injection spreads from agent to agent
threats.description: One agent reads planted content and its output carries the instruction to the orchestrator or to peers, possibly copying itself onward.
questions: Which agents read untrusted content, and what do they return to others?
Does a receiving agent treat another agent's output as data or as instruction?
vendor_evidence: Testing of injection across agent boundaries.
How inter-agent messages are framed to the model.
no_standard_test: The vendor's own orchestration. Public work uses open frameworks, not a given product.

threats.title: Delegation widens privileges
threats.description: A low-privilege agent gets a higher-privilege one to act for it, or subagents inherit the orchestrator's credentials.
questions: Does each agent have its own identity and the narrowest permissions for its job?
Are credentials passed down, and are they scoped to the subtask?
vendor_evidence: The identity and permission model for subagents.
no_standard_test: Design review. No benchmark of a product's delegation model.

threats.title: A message or an agent is not who it claims to be
threats.description: Messages between agents are not authenticated, or an unknown agent joins and is trusted.
questions: How does an agent know which agent sent a message?
Who can register an agent, and is there an allowlist?
vendor_evidence: Authentication between agents and of remote agents.

threats.title: One failure cascades
threats.description: An error, a loop or a compromised agent is amplified through the chain: repeated actions, runaway cost, wide damage.
questions: What limits depth, fan-out, retries and spend?
What stops a chain when one agent misbehaves?

threats.title: Context is over-shared between agents
threats.description: The orchestrator passes its whole context, including secrets and personal data, to a subagent that has outbound tools or runs elsewhere.
questions: What context does each subagent receive?
Do any subagents run on another vendor's infrastructure?
vendor_evidence: How context is partitioned between agents.

threats.title: Nobody can say which agent did what
threats.description: Logs are split per agent, approvals attach to the wrong step, and an agent acting outside its role goes unnoticed.
questions: Is there one trace across all agents for a request?
Where do human approvals sit, and what do they show?
vendor_evidence: Tracing and audit features across agents.
no_standard_test: No standard test. Record what is in place.

threats.title: Agents supplied by others
threats.description: An agent you call is built or operated by a third party, and can change.
questions: Which agents come from outside, and who vets them?
vendor_evidence: Provenance and review of third-party agents.
